title: XXE Practice Lab
text: Download the vulnerable PHP lab and payload collection.
Blind XXE occurs when the server parses attacker-controlled XML and expands external entities, but does NOT reflect the processed XML in the HTTP response.

code:
<?php
$xml = file_get_contents("php://input");

$dom = new DOMDocument();
$dom->loadXML($xml, LIBXML_NOENT | LIBXML_DTDLOAD);

echo "Processed";
?>

text: The XML is parsed with entity expansion enabled, but the processed XML is NOT returned. Therefore, entity output cannot be seen directly.
%file reads and base64-encodes the target file. %evil dynamically creates a new entity that forces the server to send the file content to the attacker server.
The payload loads the external DTD from the attacker. The DTD injects the exfil entity. The &exfil; reference triggers the outbound request.
The victim first requests evil.dtd. Then it sends a second request containing base64-encoded file data as a query parameter.

title: How Blind XXE Executes
items: External DTD is fetched from attacker.
Server makes outbound HTTP request with file data.

title: Conditions for Blind XXE
items: External entity expansion must be allowed.
Outbound network requests must be permitted.

text: Raw file content may contain newlines and special characters that break the HTTP request. Base64 ensures safe transmission inside a URL.

title: Common Practical Limitations
items: Outbound traffic filtering may block exfiltration.
Modern parsers often disable DTD processing by default.
WAF may block suspicious DOCTYPE usage.

text: Blind XXE allows attackers to extract sensitive data even when the application does not reflect parsed XML. Data exfiltration occurs through outbound requests triggered by entity expansion.
